title: Procedural Reliability Safeguards for AI Assisted Digital Evidence Analysis in Bangladesh
content: AI assisted digital evidence analysis requires safeguards that connect technical performance with legally examinable procedures. This study examines whether endorsement of independent validation and chain of custody is accompanied by endorsement of methodological documentation and human expert review in a Bangladesh based survey. The cross-sectional database contains 385 adult, AI aware respondents, including 253 law students, 67 law graduates and 32 advocates or legal professionals. Five digital evidence statements were analysed separately because their content combines perceived screening usefulness with distinct procedural requirements and does not establish a reflective reliability scale. Analyses comprise item distributions, six paired endorsement comparisons with Holm adjustment, joint response patterns, and two adjusted logistic models with robust covariance estimates. Independent validation was endorsed by 79.5% and chain of custody by 81.8%, compared with 59.0% for documentation and 63.4% for expert review. The four comparisons across these two pairs differed by 16.1-22.9 percentage points, with adjusted p values below .001. Only 29.4% endorsed all four safeguards. Validation endorsement was not clearly associated with documentation endorsement after adjustment (odds ratio 1.06, 95% interval 0.80-1.41) or review endorsement (0.94, 0.70-1.28). These findings identify uneven endorsement of complementary safeguards within this sample, rather than actual forensic reliability, national professional opinion or causal effects. Read alongside Bangladesh’s digital record and expert evidence provisions, the results support education and reporting practices that connect validation and custody to inspectable methods and competent review. The study contributes an item-specific account of procedural reliability expectations while retaining explicit boundaries between survey attitudes, technical accuracy and legal admissibility.
